claim: Vagus nerve stimulation reduces seizure frequency by 50% or more in approximately half of implanted patients.
evidence: Drug-resistant epilepsy is defined as the failure of adequate trials of two tolerated and appropriately chosen antiseizure medications to achieve sustained seizure freedom.

claim: Superior quadrantanopia occurs in a subset of patients following temporal lobectomy due to Meyer's loop disruption.
evidence: Surgical anterior temporal lobectomy or selective amygdalohippocampectomy results in long-term seizure freedom in 60% to 80% of well-selected patients with unilateral drug-resistant temporal lobe epilepsy.

claim: Ethosuximide is the first-line pharmacotherapy for childhood absence epilepsy due to low neuropsychological side effects.
evidence: The electroencephalographic hallmark of typical absence seizures is bilateral, synchronous, and symmetrical 3 Hz spike-and-wave discharges against a normal background.

claim: Valproate-induced hyperammonemic encephalopathy can occur with normal liver function enzymes.
evidence: Valproate possesses multiple mechanisms including voltage-gated sodium channel inhibition and GABAergic enhancement, conferring broad-spectrum efficacy in absence, myoclonic, and tonic-clonic generalized seizures.

claim: High-dose folic acid supplementation is recommended prior to conception for women prescribed antiseizure medications.
evidence: In utero exposure to valproate is associated with a high incidence of major congenital malformations, notably neural tube defects, as well as impaired cognitive and developmental outcomes in offspring.

claim: Sleep deprivation and alcohol consumption are frequent lifestyle triggers for myoclonic seizures.
evidence: Juvenile myoclonic epilepsy is an idiopathic generalized epilepsy syndrome characteristically presenting in adolescence with awakening myoclonic jerks of the upper extremities and frequent electroencephalographic photosensitivity.
